instances.title: transfer a specific token through smart contract
instances.why: Standard SEP-41 payout idiom: build a token::Client for a stored token address, then call .transfer twice to split a reward between user and treasury.

instances.title: authorize nested smart contract call
instances.why: env.authorize_as_current_contract with an InvokerContractAuthEntry::Contract(SubContractInvocation) so the contract's own auth covers a token transfer performed inside a downstream Blend call.

instances.title: calling Blend Protocol (testnet)
instances.why: Hand-written Blend pool client: PoolClient::new(env, &pool_addr) then .submit() with a request list whose token transfer was pre-authorized just above.

instances.title: working Blend Protocol interface file
instances.why: Complete hand-written client module for Blend's pool contract (Request type, submit/withdraw wrappers); the companion interface to the call site above.

instances.title: calling DeFindex Protocol (testnet)
instances.why: DefindexClient::new(env, &vault) then read total_supply()/fetch_total_managed_funds() to price shares before client.withdraw(shares, min_amounts_out, to).

instances.title: working DeFindex Protocol interface file
instances.why: Complete hand-written client module for a DeFindex vault; same pattern as the Blend client, useful as a template for writing your own interface file.

instances.title: bumping the storage
instances.why: storage.extend_ttl on persistent entries to keep vault and reward data alive; the routine 'bump' every contract with persistent state needs.

instances.title: call the XLM token from a contract, the shortcut way
instances.why: stellar_registry::import_contract!(env, xlm) resolves the XLM SAC address at build time and returns a ready-made token client for free; see tip() further down for the .transfer call.

instances.title: call a contract with try_invoke_contract
instances.why: Hand-rolled client module for the project's own DID-registry contract: address set at runtime, panics caught as Err instead of propagated, and the response decoded as an opaque Val/Map without generated types.
